::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Fastest way to compute a determinant from a LaTeX matrix input](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/2650941/fastest-way-to-compute-a-determinant-from-a-latex-matrix-input), asked by [Basj](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/109021/basj) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2018-02-14; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I have this input, coming from a LaTeX document:
>
> ```
> \begin{pmatrix}
> 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 
> -2 & 2 & 3 & 4 \\ 
> -1 & 2 & -1 & 3 \\ 
> 0 & 1 & 3 & 1
> \end{pmatrix}
> ```
>
> What's the shortest path to get its determinant, with a PC/Windows?
>
> 1. Use an online service (which one) ?
>
> 2. Import it to Maple (my Maple 7 doesn't seem to recognize it when I copy/paste this LaTeX)
>
> 3. Another software available on this platform? (that can do this in a few clicks: import from LaTeX, compute determinant, display result)
>
>
> Note: I don't want to have to manually copy each coefficient into a new Maple matrix / don't want to manually copy each coefficient into an online tool; I was looking for something that would work with a copy/paste of the LaTeX definition of the matrix.
:::

[Wolfram Alpha reads LaTeX input syntax](https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i2d=true&i=%5Cbegin%5C%28123%29pmatrix%5C%28125%29%0A1+%26+2+%26+3+%26+4+%5C%5C+%0A-2+%26+2+%26+3+%26+4+%5C%5C+%0A-1+%26+2+%26+-1+%26+3+%5C%5C+%0A0+%26+1+%26+3+%26+1%0A%5Cend%5C%28123%29pmatrix%5C%28125%29).
